about.title: Our Background
about.buildingCaption: Our school building in Patarasi-3, Jumla. Opened in 2023.
about.motto: Learn with wisdom, lead with compassion.
about.mottoText: Education isn't just about gathering knowledge. It's about building wisdom and sound thinking. Good leadership starts with a compassionate heart, serving and guiding others so students grow into people who help not just themselves, but their whole community.
about.intro: Manju Shree Primary School is located in Patarasi-3, Jumla. It opened in 2023 in a traditional stone building at the heart of the village, and has quickly grown into a school known for academic excellence and cultural preservation.
about.howWeStartedP1: Manju Shree Primary School opened in 2023 in a traditional stone building in Patarasi-3, Jumla. Supported by local community members, Buddhist monks, and international partners, the school held a joyful opening ceremony that welcomed the village's children to a place built especially for them.
about.howWeStartedP2: Just a few years in, the school is already home to a close-knit community of students, teachers, and volunteers. Kind individuals and local partners have stepped in to help make sure every student has the supplies they need.

founded.text: Shree Manju Shree Primary School opened in a traditional stone building in the heart of Patarasi-3, Jumla.

campus.text: Celebrated our opening ceremony with blessings from local Buddhist monks and the whole community.

language.text: Introduced Sambata as an additional language and culture elective alongside our core curriculum.

programs.text: Partnered with kind individuals and local volunteers to provide school bags and supplies to every student.

today.text: 135+ students across all primary grades, supported by 12 teachers and a growing network of local and international volunteers.

about.goalsSubtitle: Everything we do is guided by four core commitments to our students and community.

quality.title: Deliver quality education for every child
quality.description: Provide a well-rounded, affordable education regardless of a family's financial background.

language.title: Preserve our tradition and culture
language.description: Ensure the next generation stays connected to their roots, customs, and heritage, and takes pride in who they are.

confidence.title: Build confident, capable young people
confidence.description: Develop critical thinking, creativity, and life skills that prepare students for higher education and beyond.

community.title: Strengthen the community around the school
community.description: Partner with families and volunteers so no child goes without food, hygiene essentials, or school supplies.

about.valuesSubtitle: Six values that we teach, model, and live by every day.

respect.title: Respect
respect.description: We treat every student, family, and colleague with dignity and kindness.

integrity.title: Integrity
integrity.description: We act honestly and hold ourselves accountable, in and out of the classroom.

compassion.title: Compassion
compassion.description: We care for the wellbeing of every child, especially those who need it most.

curiosity.title: Curiosity
curiosity.description: We encourage questions, exploration, and a lifelong love of learning.

community.title: Community
community.description: We believe education is a shared responsibility between school, family, and volunteers.

perseverance.title: Perseverance
perseverance.description: We teach students to work hard, stay resilient, and never give up on their goals.

curriculum.title: Our Curriculum
curriculum.subtitle: We follow the government's national curriculum in math, science, and the arts. We also offer Sambata as a language and culture elective, much like a school elsewhere might offer Mandarin or Vietnamese, giving every student at Manju Shree Primary School a strong foundation.
curriculum.levelsSubtitle: Taught alongside the national curriculum, our Sambata elective builds progressively from spoken foundations to advanced literature and composition.

foundation.description: Students learn the Sambata alphabet, common greetings, numbers, and everyday vocabulary through songs, games, and guided conversation.

intermediate.description: Students build grammar and comprehension skills, reading short stories and writing simple compositions in Sambata.

advanced.description: Students study Sambata literature and oral history, and practice formal writing, debate, and storytelling.

immersion.title: Immersion-first teaching
immersion.description: Classes are conducted primarily in Sambata to build natural fluency alongside grammar instruction.

storytelling.title: Storytelling & oral history
storytelling.description: Community elders and teachers share traditional stories that carry language, values, and history together.

songs.title: Songs, games & recitation
songs.description: Younger students learn vocabulary and pronunciation through music, rhymes, and interactive games.

cultural.title: Cultural connection
cultural.description: Field visits, festivals, and family involvement reinforce that language and culture are lived, not just studied.

curriculum.scheduleSubtitle: Sambata language class meets daily, with a focused theme each day.

trekking.title: Trekking & Meditation
trekking.subtitle: Jumla sits in one of Nepal's most beautiful and least-visited corners. On your days off, you're welcome to explore the trails and quiet spots around Patarasi and Jumla Bazaar, from short hilltop walks to the multi-day trek out to Rara Lake.
trekking.daySubtitle: Good for a free morning or afternoon during your stay. No permits or guides needed for these.

chandannath.title: Chandannath Temple
chandannath.description: A Shiva temple on the hill above Jumla Bazaar. The climb is short and the views over the valley are worth the sweat. A quiet place to sit for a while before heading back down.

patmara.title: Jumla to Patmara
patmara.description: A village trail through farmland and forest just outside Jumla Bazaar. Good for a half-day walk if you want to see how the surrounding villages live and farm.

gothichaur.title: Gothichaur
gothichaur.description: An open highland pasture used for grazing in the summer months. Flat, wide, and very quiet, it's a good spot to just sit and breathe for a while.

trekking.multiSubtitle: For volunteers staying longer, or coming back for a second trip. These need proper planning, so talk to us in advance if you want to fit one in.

rara.title: Rara Lake
rara.description: Nepal's largest lake, set inside Rara National Park at almost 3,000 meters. The trail crosses Danfe Lagna and Jaljala Pass before dropping down to the lake. It's the main reason people trek out this way, and it earns the trip.

sinja.title: Sinja Valley
sinja.duration: Usually added onto the Rara route
sinja.description: The valley where the Nepali language is said to have originated, once home to the old Khasa Malla kingdom. Old stone ruins, quiet villages, and a slower pace than the trail to Rara.

kanjiroba.title: Kanjiroba Himal Viewpoint
kanjiroba.description: For volunteers who want to push further west toward Dolpo. Bigger peaks, fewer people, and a longer commitment. Best planned well ahead of time.

trekking.noteText: Talk to our volunteer coordinator before planning a trek. Weather changes fast in the hills, some routes need a local guide, and trails can be closed depending on the season. We're happy to help you plan around your teaching schedule.

support.title: Help Us Build a Permanent Home for Our School
support.subtitle: Manju Shree Primary School, Jumla, Western Himalayan Region, Nepal
support.greetingText: We extend our heartfelt appreciation to every individual and organization dedicated to serving society and supporting underprivileged children with generosity and compassion. On behalf of Manju Shree Primary School, located in the remote Himalayan region of Jumla, western Nepal, we sincerely thank you for your kindness and consideration.
support.situationP1: Manju Shree Primary School was established to provide quality education to children living in a remote Himalayan region where educational opportunities are extremely limited. Our goal isn't just academic knowledge. We also want to nurture children with good moral values, compassion, discipline, and responsibility, so they can grow into capable, caring members of society.
support.situationP2: The school has been running for more than two years and currently teaches up to Grade Three, with Grades Four and Five planned next. We now have 100 students, and that number keeps growing as more families see the value of education. Despite this progress, we still don't have our own classrooms or an assembly hall, and have to operate out of rented buildings, which makes teaching harder. Even so, our teachers and students keep at it.
support.visionText: Our vision is to give every child access to quality education while developing academic excellence, strong moral character, cultural awareness, environmental responsibility, and compassion. We hope to become a school where children receive not only knowledge but also the values and life skills needed to build a meaningful future. Constructing permanent classrooms and a multipurpose hall has become one of our most urgent priorities, and with the support of compassionate donors, we believe the school can continue to grow and serve many more children.
support.philosophySubtitle: At Manju Shree Primary School, education isn't limited to textbooks. We want children to grow as whole people, developing knowledge, character, culture, and compassion together.

culture.title: Cultural & Language Education
culture.description: We encourage students to learn and appreciate their own language, history, traditions, music, and cultural heritage. This builds confidence, identity, and pride, while still respecting other cultures.

environment.title: Environmental Education
environment.description: Students learn to keep their surroundings clean, conserve water, reduce waste, and care for animals and plants. This helps them grow into responsible citizens who live in harmony with nature.

family.title: Respect for Parents & Family
family.description: We teach children to understand the love, sacrifice, and hard work of their parents, developing gratitude, respect, responsibility, and good character.

objectives: Provide equal educational opportunities for every child.
Ensure that children from poor and disadvantaged families can continue their education without interruption.
Instill good morals, compassion, discipline, and ethical values.
Preserve and promote local language, culture, and traditions.
Foster love, respect, and responsibility toward the natural environment.
Teach children to appreciate and respect the love and sacrifices of their parents.
Equip students with practical knowledge, confidence, and life skills so they can contribute positively to society.
Provide quality education locally so families who cannot afford to send children to cities in Nepal or abroad can still receive an excellent education within their own community.
support.whyP1: Many children in our region come from poor families and cannot afford quality education. Without educational opportunities, their future becomes increasingly difficult, limiting their ability to improve their lives and contribute to society.
support.whyP2: Education empowers children with knowledge, confidence, and hope. It helps preserve culture and language, promotes respect for the environment, and nurtures gratitude, compassion, and responsible citizenship. Achieving these goals requires adequate classrooms, learning facilities, educational materials, and financial support.
support.whyP3: Your generous contribution will directly help provide a safe learning environment and brighter opportunities for children living in one of Nepal's most remote Himalayan communities.
support.closingText: We sincerely request your kind support in helping us build a better future for these children. Every contribution, whether large or small, brings hope and creates lasting change in their lives. On behalf of the teachers, students, parents, and the entire Manju Shree Primary School community, we express our deepest gratitude for your kindness, generosity, and compassion.

founder.name: Khenpo Ngodrub Gyatso
founder.message: “I would like to extend my best wishes to all of you who visit the school's website. As a member of the school, I would like to say a few words. School is the source of all knowledge and skills. Education is like the eye of vision. It's hard to get anywhere without eyes. Especially in the 21st century, education is indispensable. It is very important and valuable. Therefore, Khenpo Bkalbzang Tsering said: Through hard work and dedication, Because of the poor educational environment in the country The future of the nation's lifeblood, the owner of the country's children's future. Knowing that he started this school, Dear students, I wish you all the best in your parents' future. Pay close attention and As a teacher, I don't just think it's my life's work. It is important to remember to teach the students with the responsibility of their education and future. As a member, please support us as much as you can. Thank you”

principal.name: Karna Bohora
principal.message: “श्री मञ्जुश्री आवासीय विद्यालय : ज्ञान, संस्कार र सफलताको उज्यालो यात्रा। जुम्लाको पातारासी गाउँपालिका–३ मा अवस्थित श्री मञ्जुश्री आवासीय विद्यालय केवल शिक्षा प्रदान गर्ने संस्था मात्र नभई विद्यार्थीहरूको उज्ज्वल भविष्य निर्माण गर्ने ज्ञानको पवित्र मन्दिरका रूपमा अघि बढिरहेको छ। यस विद्यालयले शिक्षा, अनुशासन, संस्कार र नैतिक मूल्यलाई आत्मसात् गर्दै विद्यार्थीहरूको सर्वाङ्गीण विकासमा महत्वपूर्ण योगदान पुर्‍याउँदै आएको छ। विद्यालयको शैक्षिक वातावरण, शिक्षक–शिक्षिकाको समर्पण, विद्यालय व्यवस्थापनको कुशल नेतृत्व र अभिभावकहरूको निरन्तर सहयोगले विद्यार्थीहरूमा पढाइप्रतिको रुचि, मेहनत र आत्मविश्वास बढाउन महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका खेलेको छ। यहाँका विद्यार्थीहरूले अध्ययनसँगै विभिन्न अतिरिक्त क्रियाकलाप, खेलकुद तथा सिर्जनात्मक क्षेत्रमा समेत आफ्नो प्रतिभा प्रस्तुत गर्दै विद्यालयको नाम उज्यालो बनाउँदै आएका छन्। विद्यार्थीहरूको मेहनत, शिक्षकहरूको मार्गदर्शन र अभिभावकहरूको विश्वासकै परिणामस्वरूप विद्यालयले हासिल गरेका शैक्षिक तथा अन्य उपलब्धिहरू प्रशंसनीय छन्। विशेषगरी विद्यार्थीहरूको सफलता र उत्कृष्ट प्रदर्शनले 'मेहनत गरे सफलता अवश्य प्राप्त हुन्छ' भन्ने प्रेरणादायी सन्देश दिएको छ। विद्यालयमा अध्ययनरत प्रत्येक विद्यार्थीको सफलता नै विद्यालयको सबैभन्दा ठूलो उपलब्धि र गौरव हो। आजका विद्यार्थी नै भोलिका सक्षम नागरिक, राष्ट्रका कर्णधार र समाज परिवर्तनका संवाहक हुन्। त्यसैले श्री मञ्जुश्री आवासीय विद्यालयले विद्यार्थीहरूलाई केवल किताबी ज्ञानमा सीमित नराखी असल संस्कार, अनुशासन, जिम्मेवारी, आत्मनिर्भरता र मानवीय मूल्य सिकाउँदै अघि बढ्न सकेमा यसको योगदान अझ महत्वपूर्ण बन्नेछ। आगामी दिनमा आधुनिक प्रविधिमैत्री शिक्षा, गुणस्तरीय शिक्षण पद्धति, दक्ष जनशक्ति, उत्कृष्ट शैक्षिक वातावरण र विद्यार्थीको प्रतिभा विकासमा अझ बढी जोड दिँदै श्री मञ्जुश्री आवासीय विद्यालय पातारासी क्षेत्रकै उत्कृष्ट शैक्षिक गन्तव्य बन्न सफल होस् भन्ने हार्दिक शुभकामना व्यक्त गर्दछु। ज्ञानको ज्योति फैलाउँदै, संस्कारको बाटो देखाउँदै र सफलताको शिखर चुम्न प्रेरित गर्दै—श्री मञ्जुश्री आवासीय विद्यालय निरन्तर प्रगतिको यात्रामा अघि बढिरहोस्। यही नै हाम्रो शुभेच्छा, यही नै हाम्रो कामना!”

advisor.name: Sudha Shrestha
advisor.message: Manjushree Primary School may be a small primary school but it is built on a great and noble vision. Here, the children do not only study textbooks, they also learn how to become kind, compassionate, and responsible human beings. As an advisor to this wonderful school, I feel honoured to be part of this meaningful journey. My heartfelt wishes go to every teacher, staff member, student, and parent who shares this noble mission. May the school create a legacy of hope, kindness, and excellence that will be remembered for years to come.

advisor.name: Maria Suominen
advisor.title: Writer, Linguist, Artist and Teacher based in Finland, travelling the world
advisor.message:
In 2022, Kalsang visited me in Finland, a country known for its education system. He explained that children from his village in Nepal had to leave for Kathmandu or India because there were no adequate schools nearby. I pointed out that this not only meant leaving their families but also becoming separated from the Himalayan culture and way of life, ultimately contributing to depopulation in the region. The dangers they faced on the journey made it all the more alarming.

I asked Kalsang whether he had ever thought of establishing a village school. He replied that it had long been his dream, and I encouraged him to pursue it.

In 2024 we met again, in Delhi this time. Permission to establish the school had been obtained, and we drafted a preliminary curriculum and timetable. I emphasized the importance of securing the villagers' commitment and keeping the project in local hands to ensure its long-term sustainability. Outsiders could offer advice, but the locals should decide.

The school opened later that year. Seeing it flourish brings me immense joy!

Om Ah Rapatsana Dhi!
